intro.text: Solitron Devices, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Company" or "Solitron"), designs, develops, manufactures and markets solid‑state semiconductor components and related devices primarily for the military and aerospace markets. The Company manufactures a large variety of bipolar and metal oxide semiconductor ("MOS") power transistors, power and control hybrids, junction and power MOS field effect transistors ("Power MOSFETS"), field effect transistors and other related products. Most of the Company's products are custom made pursuant to contracts with customers whose end products are sold to the United States government. Other products, such as Joint Army/Navy ("JAN") transistors, diodes and Standard Military Drawings (“SMD”) voltage regulators, are sold as standard or catalog items.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

During the fiscal year ended February 28, 2026, ConMed Linvatec accounted for approximately 33% of net sales and RTX Corporation 27% of net sales.
No other customer accounted for 10% or more of net sales.
During the fiscal year ended February 28, 2025, ConMed Linvatec accounted for approximately 38% of net sales and RTX Corporation 31% of net sales.

Nine of the Company’s customers accounted for approximately 91% of the Company’s net sales during the fiscal year ended February 28, 2026, as compared to seven customers accounting for 89% of net sales for the fiscal year ended February 28, 2025.
Sales to foreign customers accounted for less than 5% of the Company’s net sales for the fiscal year ended February 28, 2026 and less than 1% for the fiscal year ended February 28, 2025.
During the fiscal year ended February 28, 2026, two customers accounted for approximately 60% of revenue.
During the fiscal year ended February 28, 2025, two customers accounted for approximately 69% of revenue.
No other customer accounted for 10% or more of accounts receivable.
For the year ended February 28, 2026 , sales to ConMed Linvatec accounted for approximately 33 % of net sales and sales to RTX accounted for approximately 27 % of net sales.
No other customer accounted for more than 10% of net sales.
For the year ended February 28, 2025 , sales to ConMed Linvatec accounted for approximately 38 % of net sales and sales to RTX accounted for 31 % of net sales.

Many of the packages are manufactured by the Company and, in most cases, the Company plates its packages with gold, nickel or other metals utilizing outside vendors to perform the plating operation .

The Company’s backlog as of any particular date may not be representative of actual sales for any succeeding period because lead times for the release of purchase orders depend upon the scheduling practices of individual customers.

The Company is not in direct competition with any other semiconductor manufacturer for an identical mixture of products; however, one or more of the major manufacturers of semiconductors manufacture some of the Company’s products.

The Company relies on its relationships with certain key suppliers for its supply of raw materials, parts and finished components that are qualified for use in the end-products the Company manufactures.
We rely on several suppliers for the purchase of materials used in the manufacture and production of our goods, including various foreign suppliers in multiple foreign jurisdictions.
In fiscal year 2026, approximately 31% of our materials were purchased from foreign suppliers, including 1% from Malaysia and 30% from China.
Our success in these markets depends on our ability to design, develop, manufacture, assemble, test, market and support new products and enhancements on a timely and cost-effective basis.
We depend on the recruitment and retention of qualified personnel and our failure to attract and retain such personnel could seriously harm our business.

Our prospects depend on our ability to attract and retain qualified engineering, manufacturing, marketing, sales and management personnel for our operations as well as conduct appropriate succession planning for our executive officers.
Certain contracts are also subject to price renegotiations in accordance with United States Government sole source procurement provisions.

We depend on the U.S. government and its suppliers for a substantial portion of our business, and changes in government defense spending and priorities could have consequences on our financial position, results of operations and business.

As a company that relies on government contracts and makes a large portion of sales in the military and aerospace markets, our business operations and revenue streams may be subject to DOGE and other administrative actions, which may introduce material risks to our financial performance and strategic growth.
